newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FORECAST-New World interim seen strong.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-New World interim seen strong.

text.p: New World Development Co Ltd is expected to post a solid increase in net profits for the six months to December 31, helped by good residential property sales and a decision to sell a Hong Kong hotel, analysts said.

"I think it will be very good as you can see (from) the property sales at Discovery Park," said Kerry Wong of Lippo Securities, who is still finalising her interim figures for the group but expects it to announce good results on Tuesday.
The Hong Kong property developer posted net profit of HK$1.70 billion in the half year to December 31, 1995, and HKK$4.16 billion for the year to June 30, 1996.
New World Development and HKR International Ltd said this month that they were selling 98 flats in the Discovery Park residential development in the New Territories at HK$5,898 per square foot.
This compares with HK$5,000 psf in their last sale in September. The Discovery Park development is a 50-50 joint venture between HKR and New World Development.
Wong also expected the company to book about HK$1 billion from the sale of the Victoria Hotel near Hong Kong's busy Central business district.
Property sales should contribute HK$1.5 billion overall to profits, and rental income another HK$700 million, said Wong.
Asia Equity analyst David Low and Daiwa Institute of Research (HK) analyst Eric Yuen were both slightly more bullish,
